_README: Measured facts about the dataset, with a STATUS saying whether each is desired.
This is a characterization ledger, not a wishlist. Several entries record values we
know are WRONG (status 'known_bad'). That is deliberate: the tool has documented
distortions, and pinning their current values turns 'we know it's broken' into a
tripwire. scripts/check.py goes RED when reality diverges from a recorded value in
EITHER direction — a fix and a regression both need a human to look.
When you fix something: run `python3 scripts/check.py`, read the CHANGED block, and
if the new number is the intended one, update `value` here and flip `status` to
'good'. Updating this file is the act of claiming a fix — do not do it casually, and
measured_on dates are when the value was last confirmed, not when it was written.

rows.why_pinned: a silent change here means the pipeline or a concat changed shape

positions.note: 3 of the PDR's 9 position groups. Missing QB/OL/DL/LB/DB/ST.

recruit_years.why_bad: PDR §3.1.4 asks for 10 classes (2015-2024); we have 7.

outcome_labels_are_percentile_buckets.what: outcome share (%) across the whole dataset
why_bad: These ARE the cut points (0.25/0.60/0.85 -> 25/35/25/15). The distribution is a
definitional artifact of percentile bucketing, not an empirical finding.
PDR §3.1.1 wants absolute standards: Starter = holds a starting role a full
season; Impact = All-Conference or draft pick.
Side effect: labels are position-RELATIVE, so a 'Starter' RB and a 'Starter' WR
are not the same thing — and that feeds straight into the dollar mapping.
outcome_labels_are_percentile_buckets.what_fixed_looks_like: shares diverge from the cut points and vary across years

outcome_shares_uniform_across_years.what: largest spread, in percentage points, of any outcome's share across eligibility years 1-5
why_bad: A real career-outcome distribution changes with eligibility year — year-1 true
freshmen should bust far more often than year-4 players. A spread near zero is
proof the labels carry no year signal, because the percentile cut is applied
outcome_shares_uniform_across_years.what_fixed_looks_like: spread grows well past 1pp; year 1 skews Bust

survivorship_non_participants_missing.what: share of pulled WR/RB/TE recruits that appear in the outcomes table
why_bad: The pipeline starts from the STATS endpoint and left-joins recruits onto it, so a
recruit who never recorded a carry or catch never enters the table. The ~58%
missing are the real busts. So 'Bust' currently means 'bottom quartile of players
Fix: invert the merge — start from the recruit list, left-join stats, treat
survivorship_non_participants_missing.what_fixed_looks_like: coverage approaches 100% and the Bust share rises sharply

no_power4_scoping.what: conference breadth of the comparable pool
why_bad: PDR §3.1.4 says scope to ACC / Power 4 where possible. Sun Belt, MAC etc. sit in
the same percentile pool and distort the ranks.

knn_ordering.why_bad: ordering and spread are sensible; the LEVELS are not (a 2-star at 17% Impact is not credible)
knn_ordering.note: relabeling under fix items 1-2 should PRESERVE the ordering. If it inverts, the fix broke the model.
knn_ordering.why_not: requires instantiating app.py's KNN model; not wired up yet. Measured by hand 2026-08-12.
